claim: The log summarizer is safe to point at very large files, meaning memory use only: it reads one line at a time, its memory does not grow with the number of lines, and summarizing two files that each end in a newline and merging gives the same figures as summarizing the two files joined together.
why: Reading is a generator over the file handle and the counters are fixed-size, so the first two parts hold. The merge part fails: the mean is kept as a running average, and merge averages the two means without weighting by count. The two sample files have five valid lines each, so they match, which hides the fault; files of different sizes give a different mean than the joined file.

deciding.pattern: (one line at a time|line by line|generator|stream)

root.claim: The summarizer is safe for very large files in the three stated ways.

atoms.claim: It reads one line at a time.
atoms.evidence: reader.load_all is a generator over `for line in handle`; summarize adds each record and keeps none.

atoms.claim: Its memory does not grow with the number of lines.
atoms.evidence: Summary holds two Counters with at most 6 and 4 keys (status class clamped to 0 through 5, bucket index 0 to 3) and three numbers.

atoms.claim: Merging per-file summaries gives the same figures as summarizing the two files joined together.
atoms.evidence: merge sets mean_ms to the plain average of the two means, ignoring counts. part1.log plus an 8-line file gives mean 477.46 when merged and 495.82 when joined; the two sample files match only because both have 5 valid lines.
